1.explanation:
1. runner-test.js  – shows how the Lighthouse runner handles flags like `--save-assets` and emits trace artifacts to disk, which is the entry point for injecting synthetic metrics.
2. gather/computed/trace-of-tab-test.js  – verifies how raw trace events (including any custom/injected ones) are parsed into the TraceOfTab artifact, essential for understanding how the synthetic metric events end up in the model.
3. gather/computed/speedline-test.js  – tests the Speedline computed artifact which processes trace screenshots and timing events, relevant for how the Perceptual Speed Index markers are derived from trace events.
4. audits/first-meaningful-paint-test.js  – contains the logic for extracting the First Meaningful Paint metric, ensuring the correct marker is generated and labeled in the UI timeline.
5. audits/speed-index-metric-test.js  – covers the computation and export of the Perceptual Speed Index metric, which is injected as a trace event and rendered in the Timeline.
6. audits/time-to-interactive-test.js  – tests the Time to Interactive audit and how it exports that metric as a trace event, corresponding to the final marker shown at ~17.4 s in the screenshot.
1.bug_scenario: The user has instrumented Lighthouse to export key performance metrics (First Contentful Paint, First Meaningful Paint, First Visual Change, Visually Complete, Perceptual Speed Index, Time to Interactive) as synthetic trace events when saving a trace (`--save-assets`). When that trace is opened in Chrome DevTools Timeline, these fake events appear as markers along the timeline (red flags) which show metric names and timestamps—for example “First meaningful paint at 3.09 s”, “Perceptual Speed Index at 8.67 s”, “Time to Interactive at 17.40 s”. The bug relates to how those injected trace events are processed by the gatherers/computed artifacts (e.g., trace-of-tab, speedline) and then surfaced in the audits (first-meaningful-paint, speed-index, time-to-interactive).
